description: A comprehensive overview of India's rich musical traditions, covering the fundamental systems of Hindustani and Carnatic classical music, prominent Gharanas, renowned instrumentalists, and regional folk music.

sections.title: Fundamentals of Classical Music
sections.description: The basic elements and the two major pillars of the Indian Classical Music system.

key_concepts.explanation: Shruti refers to the microtones that a human ear can perceive (total 22). Swara refers to the 7 main musical notes (Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni).
Raga forms the melodic framework or the soul of the music, whereas Tala represents the rhythmic cycle and time measure.
Practiced primarily in North India. It evolved and assimilated heavy Persian and Islamic influences during the Mughal and Delhi Sultanate periods.
Practiced primarily in South India. It remained largely unaffected by external influences and is preserved in its traditional and indigenous Hindu form.

sections.title: Gharanas of Hindustani Classical Music
sections.description: A 'Gharana' represents a lineage of musicians and a distinct stylistic identity of singing in Hindustani music.

key_associations.associated_with: Haddu Khan, Hassu Khan, Pt. Omkarnath Thakur
key_associations.extra_info: Considered the oldest and the mother of all Gharanas in Hindustani classical music.

key_associations.associated_with: Haji Sujan Khan, Ustad Faiyaz Khan
key_associations.extra_info: Famous for its unique 'Nom-Tom' style of Alaap and strong emphasis on rhythm (Layakari).

key_associations.associated_with: Abdul Karim Khan, Pt. Bhimsen Joshi, Gangubai Hangal
key_associations.extra_info: This Gharana places maximum emphasis on perfect intonation (purity of Swara) and slow-tempo melodies.

key_associations.associated_with: Ustad Alladiya Khan, Kishori Amonkar, Mallikarjun Mansur
key_associations.extra_info: Known for its complex, intricate, and curved musical phrases (Vakra Taans).

sections.title: Pillars of Carnatic Classical Music
sections.description: The foundational figures of the South Indian classical music system, which is highly composition-based.

key_associations.extra_info: During the 18th century, these three composer-musicians created the greatest masterworks (Kritis) of Carnatic music.

key_associations.associated_with: Revered as the 'Pitamaha' (Father of Carnatic Music)
key_associations.extra_info: He formulated the basic lessons, fundamental exercises, and teaching methodologies still used in Carnatic music today.

sections.title: Important Musical Instruments and Exponents
sections.description: Key traditional instruments of India and their world-renowned maestros.

key_associations.associated_with: Pt. Ravi Shankar, Ustad Vilayat Khan, Nikhil Banerjee
key_associations.extra_info: A popular plucked stringed instrument used mainly in Hindustani music and Indian classical crossover.

key_associations.associated_with: Ustad Alla Rakha, Ustad Zakir Hussain, Pt. Kishan Maharaj
key_associations.extra_info: The principal percussion instrument in Hindustani classical music, consisting of a pair of hand drums.

key_associations.associated_with: Ustad Bismillah Khan, Ali Ahmed Hussain Khan
key_associations.extra_info: A double-reed wind instrument traditionally considered auspicious and played during marriages and temple rituals.
A simple yet highly expressive wind instrument made from a single hollow shaft of bamboo.
Originally a folk instrument from the Kashmir valley, it is a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer with up to 100 strings.

sections.title: Major Folk Music of India
sections.description: Traditional grassroots music styles originating from various Indian states.

key_associations.extra_info: A form of mystic folk singing heavily influenced by Sufi and Vaishnava traditions, performed by wandering minstrels.
A fast-paced, energetic musical style sung to the powerful beats of the Dholki, often associated with theatrical performances.
A musical narration of tales from the Hindu epic Mahabharata. Teejan Bai is its most celebrated exponent.
A traditional river song sung by boatmen while rowing down the streams.
A popular folk genre from the Braj region that primarily depicts the divine love of Lord Krishna and Radha.

sections.title: Important Exam-Oriented Facts
sections.description: Crucial historical and general knowledge facts frequently asked in competitive exams.

important_facts.fact: The 'Samaveda' is considered the ultimate root source of Indian classical music and art forms.
The 'Natya Shastra', compiled by Sage Bharat Muni, is the oldest surviving and most authoritative ancient treatise on performing arts (music, dance, and drama).
Sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar was the first Indian to win a Grammy Award in 1968 for 'West Meets East'.
Legendary Carnatic vocalist M. S. Subbulakshmi was the first musician ever to be awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honor, in 1998.
Dhrupad is the oldest surviving form of Hindustani classical music, famously patronized by Raja Mansingh Tomar of Gwalior and later by Emperor Akbar (sung by Tansen).
